class.name: HDWISPIResource
class.brief_description: Virtual SPI peripheral on a (bus, chip-select) - models a full-duplex MOSI/MISO device such as an MS5803 pressure sensor.
class.description:
Represents one SPI slave addressed by ([member bus_index], [member chip_select_line]). SPI is full duplex: every transfer the FSW pushes N MOSI bytes and expects N MISO bytes back in the same exchange. This resource hands the MOSI bytes to GDScript via [signal on_spi_transfer] and ships back whatever GDScript leaves in [member miso_buffer]. [b]How to interface[/b] [olist] [*]Set the addressing/config properties: [member bus_index], [member chip_select_line], [member mode], [member bits_per_word], [member max_speed_hz]. (When the FSW configures the bus these get overwritten from the [signal on_spi_setup] data.) [*]Call [method HDWIResource.init] to register the device. [*]Connect [signal on_spi_transfer]. In the handler, compute the device's MISO response and call [method set_miso_buffer] [b]synchronously[/b] - the handler runs inline before the response is framed and sent, so the stream desyncs if you defer it. [*]Connect [signal HDWIResource.on_send] to forward the framed MISO response to the kernel socket. [/olist] [b]Example - an MS5803 returning its response to each command[/b] [codeblock] var spi = HDWISPIResource.new() spi.device_name = "ms5803" spi.bus_index = 0 spi.chip_select_line = 0 spi.mode = 0 spi.bits_per_word = 8 spi.max_speed_hz = 1_000_000 spi.init()
spi.on_spi_setup.connect(_on_setup) spi.on_spi_transfer.connect(_on_transfer) spi.on_send.connect(_write_to_kernel_socket)
func _on_setup(mode, bits_per_word, speed_hz): print("FSW configured SPI: mode=%d bpw=%d speed=%d" % [mode, bits_per_word, speed_hz])
func _on_transfer(tx_data): # tx_data = MOSI bytes from the FSW. Build N MISO bytes in reply. var miso = PackedByteArray() miso.resize(tx_data.size()) miso[0] = 0x00 # device-specific response to tx_data spi.set_miso_buffer(miso) # MUST be set before this handler returns [/codeblock] If you set a MISO buffer of the wrong length it is clamped/padded to the transfer size; the default is N zero bytes.

method.name: handle_spi_setup
method.description: Internal. Decodes an 8-byte SPI setup payload (mode, bits-per-word, speed) into the matching properties and emits [signal on_spi_setup]. Invoked by [method HDWIResource.dispatch_action] on a [code]SPI_SETUP[/code] action.

method.name: handle_spi_transfer
method.description: Internal. Takes N raw MOSI bytes, emits [signal on_spi_transfer] (synchronous, so GDScript can fill [member miso_buffer]), then frames the MISO buffer and emits [signal HDWIResource.on_send]. Invoked on a [code]SPI_TRANSFER[/code] action.

method.name: get_group_type_representation
method.description: Builds the SPI section of the [code]CMD_SYNCH[/code] registration body, grouping registered devices by [member bus_index]. Called by the registry during sync.

method.name: lookup_spi_device_id
method.description: Returns the 0-based registry slot of the device at ([param bus_index], [param chip_select]), or [code]-1[/code] if none is registered.

members.member: SPI bus number this device lives on (inner SPI header [code]bus_index[/code]). Part of the routing key.
Chip-select line that selects this slave on its bus (inner SPI header [code]chip_select[/code]). Together with [member bus_index] it uniquely identifies the device.
SPI mode 0-3 (CPOL/CPHA). Overwritten when the FSW issues a setup.
Bits per SPI word (typically 8). Overwritten when the FSW issues a setup.
Maximum clock frequency in Hz. Informational on the sim side; overwritten on setup.
The MISO bytes returned for the current transfer. Fill this inside the [signal on_spi_transfer] handler. Length must equal the transfer's MOSI length (it is clamped/padded otherwise).

signal.name: on_spi_setup
signal.description: Emitted when the FSW configures the bus. The properties [member mode], [member bits_per_word], [member max_speed_hz] are already updated to these values.

signal.name: on_spi_transfer
signal.description: Emitted on each full-duplex transfer with the FSW's MOSI bytes. Fill [member miso_buffer] (via [method set_miso_buffer]) with the same number of bytes before the handler returns - the response is framed and sent the instant this signal returns.
